An Euclidean space is a [[metric space]] of real vectors with the Euclidean metric function.

[[Category:Proper name]]

== Formal definition ==

Let $S=\{\vec u=(u_1,\cdots,u_n)|u_1,\cdots,u_n \in \mathbb{R}\}$ be a set.

Define [[metric space#Formal_definition|metric function]] $d: S \times S \to \mathbb{R}$

$$
d(\vec u,\vec v)=\sqrt{(u_1-v_1)^2+\cdots+(u_n-v_n)^2},\, \forall \vec u, \vec v \in S
$$

Then $d$ is the '''Euclidean metric function''' of dimension $n$, $(S,d)$ is an '''$n$-diemensional Euclidean space'''.

{{Hidden example}}
The 3D-Euclidean space $(S=\mathbb{R}^3,d)$ is often used to model our physical world, where

$$
S=\{\vec p=(x,y,z)|x,y,z \in \mathbb{R}\}, \\
d(\vec p_1,\vec p_2)=\sqrt{(x_1-x_2)^2+(y_1-y_2)^2+(z_1-z_2)^2}.
$$

and $\vec p$ are the '''position vectors''' of points in space.
{{End hidden}}

<blockquote>
Although 3-dimensional Euclidean space is often simply referred to as 'Euclidean space', this can be a source of ambiguity. It is therefore preferred to call it 3D-Euclidean space.
</blockquote>
